result.topic_en: Tables giving, for a prime 2p+1 in various residue classes, whether it divides a^p − 1 or a^p + 1, for a = 5, 6, 7, 8 (with a = 10 introduced). This is a quadratic-residue criterion.

items.quote: Sin autem habeat formam $12n \mp 5$, per eum diuisibilis erit formula $3^p+1$.
items.english: But if it has the form 12n ∓ 5, the formula 3^p + 1 will be divisible by it.

items.quote: Sumto $a=5$, si $2p+1$ fuerit numerus primus, vtrum per eum diuisibilis sit siue formula $5^p-1$, siue $5^p+1$, sequens tabella declarat
items.english: Taking a = 5, if 2p+1 is a prime number, the following table shows whether 5^p − 1 or 5^p + 1 is divisible by it: 20n∓1 and 20n∓9 divide 5^p − 1; 20n∓3 and 20n∓7 divide 5^p + 1.

items.english: Taking a = 6, if 2p+1 is prime, the table shows: 24n±1 and 24n±5 divide 6^p − 1; 24n±7 and 24n±11 divide 6^p + 1.
